children: , the AI-focused cloud provider, to Overweight from Neutral and raised its December 2027 price target to $125 from $120, implying about 42% upside. Analyst Samik Chatterjee argued that stronger compute pricing and a push into short-term contracts at premium rates should lift both revenue and margins. CoreWeave shares were up 0.63% in premarket.
Chatterjee said demand has strengthened this year and pushed prices higher, pointing to 25% price changes across CoreWeave's products in July and frequent increases at rival Nebius

. Short-term compute pricing at some rivals is running at nearly three times what CoreWeave charges on longer-term contracts, and CoreWeave has said fiscal third-quarter contracts came in at about $40 million per megawatt. Management has also said the higher pricing adds 5 to 10 percentage points to contribution margins on new contracts, which Chatterjee sees as "dispelling any concerns that the higher price is purely a pass-through of higher costs."

The bank acknowledged concerns over how much capital CoreWeave needs to build capacity, but believes higher pricing and margins will outweigh the extra debt. JPMorgan also noted the stock has traded in a narrow range this year, even as CoreWeave raised every part of its 2026 outlook and grew contracted power to 4.2 gigawatts as of Aug. 11, up from 3.1 gigawatts at the end of 2025. The target accounts for dilution from the company's at-the-market share offering.

title: CoreWeave Wins JPMorgan Upgrade on Premium Compute Pricing
